subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app adopt a chat-first default or mode, accept focused UX/media/connectivity slices while preserving the Overview-first companion app, or keep this direction external for now?
rationale: Current main partially improves Android chat access, but changing the default surface or broader media/connectivity scope affects onboarding, pairing, permissions, security posture, and Android product direction.

options.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices with real-device proof before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Keep Overview-first
options.body: Document that the official app remains a Gateway companion with Overview-first navigation and ask contributors to file only narrow defects or owner-approved UX improvements.

options.title: Sponsor chat-first mode
options.body: Have maintainers explicitly sponsor a chat-first default or mode and require upgrade, onboarding, media-permission, and real-device proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices with real-device proof before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The Android app ownership and the feature history both point to this handle as the best first reviewer for the official Android product shape.
